title: Sharp dedicated-pool throughput cliff during autoscaler cooldown; long-lived neighbor replica holding GPU slot
text:
Sharp dedicated-pool throughput cliff during autoscaler cooldown; long-lived neighbor replica holding GPU slot

description:
Issue summary:
ScribeLabs reported a ~65% drop in throughput for their dedicated pool in us-west during a midday burst window. The regression coincided with the autoscaler entering a cooldown/hysteresis window after a short spike. Multiple customer routes experienced serialized short-stream batches and p99 token latency moved from ~180ms to ~1.2s.

Impact:
- Customer-facing routes degraded across three production services (increased latency, tail tokens lost to timeouts).
- Observed sustained lower batch concurrency for ~14 minutes until autoscaler recovered.
- No error 5xx spike, but elevated application-level timeouts and queued requests.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity, us-west, reserved pool for ScribeLabs (tier: dedicated).
- Model traffic: mix of short streaming chatlets and medium-length embeddings.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Induce short burst from a separate tenant in same reserved pool (simulated by load test).
2) Autoscaler scales up then immediately enters cooldown window.
3) A long-lived replica from an adjacent tenant retains a GPU slot with a persistent background KV-prefetch process; slot not released quickly.
4) Batcher serialization appears as short streams are queued behind the pinned slot and throughput collapses.

Observed behavior:
- GPU slot held by process pid=22311 from tenant `edge-analytics` for ~12 minutes (continuous CUDA context reported).
- Prefetch/KV cache writer logged periodic heavy io; sidecar logs show repeated keepalive + minor page faults.
- Autoscaler did not trigger an immediate additional allocation because cooldown prevented scale-out for ~90s intervals, causing sequential allocation attempts and transient underprovisioning.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived background processes should not prevent GPU slot lease reclamation during autoscale events.
- Autoscaler cooldown should be adaptive to clear evidence of held-but-idle slots to avoid prolonged underprovisioning.

Initial triage summary:
- Hypothesis: noisy neighbor (long-lived background replica) + conservative autoscale cooldown produced a window of slot starvation and batch serialization.
- Evidence: GPU allocation traces, sidecar logs, and allocator-heartbeat metrics align with the hypothesis.

Attachments: links to monitoring snapshots and a small log excerpt are in investigation notes.

investigation_notes:
Telemetry snapshots: allocator/attach traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alloc/us-west?orgId=1&from=2026-03-10T16:30:00Z&to=2026-03-10T16:50:00Z
Sidecar logs snippet: [us-west/pool-72] 2026-03-10T16:36:12Z pid=22311 keepalive prefetch_writer: bytes_written=12.3MB io_wait=18ms NVML_handle=1
GPU NVML timeline shows continuous handle present from 16:35:40 -> 16:47:55. During this window allocator reported pending batchers=3 but available_slots=0.
Autoscaler timeline: scaled +2 at 16:34, then entered cooldown. Next scale decision evaluated at 16:36 and 16:38 but conservative policy suppressed allocation due to cooldown hysteresis flag. Canary tweak proposed to add override when allocator reports 'held_slots' > 0.
Hypothesis validated by repro: replayed neighbor background prefetch in staging along with short chatlet bursts; when we force-evicted the pinned replica, throughput recovered and batches parallelized.
Related Slack threads: #support (ScribeLabs) https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C08S9K1T4/p167846... and #sre-uswest https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C1SRE1234/p167847...
Potential root causes: (1) background prefetcher not yielding GPU access when idle, (2) autoscaler cooldown too coarse-grained to detect held-but-unused slots, (3) allocator lease timeout longer than expected under mixed short/long streams.
Risk assessment: Without mitigation, similar short bursts can create repeated 5-15 minute throughput cliffs for other dedicated tenants sharing pools.
Next steps in investigation: capture per-tenant NVML hold events, instrument allocator with held_slot count metric, and add test case for background replica eviction in our CI loadbench.
Runbook links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Slot+Eviction+Procedure

resolution:
Workaround applied: performed a controlled soft-eviction of the noisy neighbor replica which freed the GPU slot and restored throughput. Autoscaler cooldown experiment (reduced strictness when held_slots>0) has been deployed to canary in us-west.

Planned permanent fixes:
- Add allocator metric 'held_slots' and an alert when > threshold during cooldown.
- Implement autoscaler override to allow immediate scale-out if held_slots prevents utilization.
- Add a probe to sidecar that detects long-running prefetche/writer loops and signals lease release earlier.
- Follow-up postmortem to be created and shared with ScribeLabs; schedule a customer-facing RCA meeting next week.
